product: Omnissa Workspace ONE / Horizon (digital workspace: unified endpoint management, virtual desktops)
vendor: Omnissa (formerly VMware End-User Computing; owned by KKR)
green_flags:
- Omnissa launched in July 2024 as an independent company, carved out of VMware/Broadcom and owned by KKR, with $1.5B in annual recurring revenue (ARR) and 26,000 customers at launch. Source says: "with $1.5 billion in annual recurring revenue and 26,000 customers around the world" https://www.omnissa.com/insights/official-launch-pr/#:~:text=with%20%241.5%20billion%20in,customers%20around%20the%20world
- Independent trade press confirms KKR completed the acquisition and the company started with more than 4,000 employees. Source says: "This acquisition took over two years to complete, and the new company has over 4,000 employees." https://virtualizationreview.com/articles/2024/07/18/omnissa.aspx#:~:text=This%20acquisition%20took%20over,has%20over%204%2C000%20employees.
- The site names its contracting entity and a physical address in the footer. Source says: "© 2026 Omnissa, LLC, 590 E Middlefield Road, Mountain View CA 94043, All Rights Reserved" https://www.omnissa.com/#:~:text=%C2%A9%202026%20Omnissa%2C%20LLC%2C,94043%2C%20All%20Rights%20Reserved
- The cloud services (Horizon Cloud, Workspace ONE UEM, Omnissa Access, Intelligence) are listed as ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701 certified. Source says: "ISO certification represents the achievement of ISO 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 standards." https://www.omnissa.com/trust-center/compliance/ISO#:~:text=ISO%20certification%20represents%20the,27018%20and%2027701%20standards.
- Omnissa claims 26,000 customers today, the same figure it gave at its 2024 launch; it has not inflated the number over time. Source says: "26,000 customers worldwide #1 in all four use cases Gartner Critical Capabilities for Endpoint Management Tools" https://www.omnissa.com/#:~:text=26%2C000%20customers%20worldwide%20%231,for%20Endpoint%20Management%20Tools
yellow_flags:
- ISO certification covers only the cloud-services management system, not on-premises Horizon 8 or self-hosted Workspace ONE. Buyers of on-premises products need a separate security review. Source says: "Our ISO certification only covers the Cloud Services Information Security Management System" https://www.omnissa.com/trust-center/compliance/ISO#:~:text=Our%20ISO%20certification%20only,Information%20Security%20Management%20System
- Private-equity ownership: KKR paid about $4B. That points to the usual risks of a PE carve-out (price pressure, cost cutting, a future sale), so negotiate renewal caps. Source says: "So technically the shareholders of KKR own Omnissa." https://www.techtarget.com/searchvirtualdesktop/opinion/Who-owns-Omnissa-and-whats-next-for-this-vendor#:~:text=So%20technically%20the%20shareholders%20of%20KKR%20own%20Omnissa.
- In March 2026 CISA added a 2021 Workspace ONE UEM server-side request forgery flaw to its exploited-in-the-wild list. VMware patched it in 2021, so the risk is unpatched on-premises consoles; confirm yours are on fixed versions. Source says: "CISA orders federal agencies to fix the vulnerabilities CVE-2026-1603 and CVE-2021-22054 by March 23, 2026." https://securityaffairs.com/189172/security/u-s-cisa-adds-ivanti-epm-solarwinds-and-omnissa-workspace-one-flaws-to-its-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog.html#:~:text=CISA%20orders%20federal%20agencies,by%20March%2023%2C%202026.
- A PeerSpot reviewer reports that support and documentation have got worse since the move from VMware to Omnissa. Ask for support commitments. Source says: "However, since becoming Omnissa, the documentation and support have become very weak compared to what we had with VMware." https://www.peerspot.com/products/vmware-workspace-one-reviews#:~:text=However%2C%20since%20becoming%20Omnissa%2C,we%20had%20with%20VMware.
- PeerSpot reviewers find Workspace ONE expensive next to Microsoft Intune, and its PeerSpot mindshare is falling. Benchmark pricing against Intune. Source says: "often find the solution expensive compared to alternatives like MobileIron or Intune" https://www.peerspot.com/products/vmware-workspace-one-reviews#:~:text=often%20find%20the%20solution,like%20MobileIron%20or%20Intune
- The homepage covers the whole portfolio (Platform, Horizon 8, Horizon Cloud, Workspace ONE UEM, Elara, Sovereign Solution), so the buyer must name the exact product and licence. Several names came over from VMware. Source says: "Horizon® Virtual desktops and apps across cloud and on-prem. Horizon 8 Horizon Cloud Workspace ONE® Unified endpoint management" https://www.omnissa.com/#:~:text=Horizon%C2%AE%20Virtual%20desktops%20and,ONE%C2%AE%20Unified%20endpoint%20management
reasoning:
What decided it: Long-established, actively developed products from a company whose ownership and legal entity are independently confirmed, with nothing found that contradicts what the vendor says.

Shortlist it. Omnissa is VMware's former End-User Computing business, which KKR bought from Broadcom for about $4 billion in July 2024. Its products are Horizon and Workspace ONE, long-established enterprise products that are still actively developed. Independent press confirms the ownership, the site names its contracting party (Omnissa, LLC in Mountain View), and the cloud services carry ISO 27001/27017/27018/27701 certification. Yellow flags to handle in negotiation: private-equity ownership, so press for renewal price caps; user reports that support and documentation got worse after leaving VMware, along with falling mindshare; ISO scope limited to the cloud services; and a 2021 Workspace ONE UEM flaw that CISA added to its exploited-in-the-wild list in March 2026, so confirm on-premises consoles are patched. The homepage covers the whole portfolio, so name the exact product and licence (e.g. Horizon 8 or Horizon Cloud, Workspace ONE UEM) in the quote.

What would change the call: It would drop to yellow if a recent, undisclosed breach of Omnissa's cloud services turned up, or a major customer-facing restructuring or end-of-life notice for Horizon or Workspace ONE. It would also drop if a regulator action, or continued business in Russia after VMware's 2022 exit, were confirmed.

product: Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat (free web-grounded AI chat for business users)
green_flags:
- Prompts and responses are covered by Microsoft's Data Protection Addendum and Product Terms, with Microsoft as data processor. Microsoft states they are not used to train foundation models. Source says: "apply to customer data for users of Microsoft Copilot and Copilot Chat, with Microsoft acting as a data processor" https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/privacy-and-protections#:~:text=apply%20to%20customer%20data,as%20a%20data%20processor
- Clifford Chance, a logo on the page, confirms on its own site that it deployed Copilot firm-wide. The customer wall is real. Source says: "with the deployment of Copilot for Microsoft 365 and Viva Suite for its employees globally." https://www.cliffordchance.com/news/news/2024/02/clifford-chance-generative-ai-microsoft.html#:~:text=with%20the%20deployment%20of,for%20its%20employees%20globally.
- The product is live and included free for eligible Microsoft 365 tenants, with an actively maintained privacy and architecture document. Source says: "Copilot Chat is available at no additional cost for all Microsoft Entra account users" https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/features/chat#:~:text=Copilot%20Chat%20is%20available,Microsoft%20Entra%20account%20users
- Microsoft suspended new sales in Russia in 2022 and scaled down operations there. The Russian-language version of the page that the script flagged is not a sign of ongoing sales. Source says: "the suspension of new sales that was announced earlier in March remains in effect." https://www.cnbc.com/2022/06/08/microsoft-scales-down-russia-operations-due-to-ukraine-crisis-.html#:~:text=the%20suspension%20of%20new,March%20remains%20in%20effect.
yellow_flags:
- Microsoft's own documentation says the product has just been renamed again, and that licences and experiences may still carry the old names during the transition. Buyers will meet several names for the same SKU. Source says: "Microsoft 365 Copilot is now named Microsoft Copilot, and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat is now named Microsoft Copilot Chat." https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/privacy-and-protections#:~:text=Microsoft%20365%20Copilot%20is,named%20Microsoft%20Copilot%20Chat.
- Independent Microsoft-licensing analysts say the name does not match how the product is licensed, and warn commercial customers about Microsoft's shifting Copilot strategy. Source says: "lack of a cohesive, consistent strategy around this set of technologies should inspire caution among commercial customers" https://www.directionsonmicrosoft.com/blog/microsoft-changes-directions-with-copilot-branding-delivery-yet-again/#:~:text=lack%20of%20a%20cohesive%2C,caution%20among%20commercial%20customers
- Paid features come in through metered agents that need an Azure subscription, on top of a per-user add-on with a promotional price. The total cost depends on usage and is hard to predict. Source says: "Access and use agents, priced on a metered basis" https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/features/chat#:~:text=Access%20and%20use%20agents%2C,on%20a%20metered%20basis
- A code error let Copilot Chat's work tab summarise emails labelled confidential, bypassing DLP, from January 2026. Microsoft disclosed it in an admin notice and deployed a fix worldwide. Source says: "Users' email messages with a confidential label applied are being incorrectly processed by Microsoft 365 Copilot chat," https://www.theregister.com/2026/02/18/microsoft_copilot_data_loss_prevention/#:~:text=Users%27%20email%20messages%20with,Microsoft%20365%20Copilot%20chat%2C
- Web-grounding queries go to Bing, outside the EU Data Boundary, with Microsoft acting as an independent controller. EU or regulated buyers should decide whether to turn web grounding off. Source says: "Web search queries sent from Copilot Chat to Bing are not EUDB-compliant." https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/privacy-and-protections#:~:text=Web%20search%20queries%20sent,Bing%20are%20not%20EUDB%2Dcompliant.
- EchoLeak (CVE-2025-32711) was a critical zero-click data-exfiltration flaw in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Microsoft fixed it on the server side and customers did not need to act. Source says: "a patch has been implemented on the server side and no customer action is required" https://www.securityweek.com/echoleak-ai-attack-enabled-theft-of-sensitive-data-via-microsoft-365-copilot/#:~:text=a%20patch%20has%20been,customer%20action%20is%20required
- Australia's ACCC is suing Microsoft over how Copilot was bundled into consumer Microsoft 365 plans and the price rises that came with it. The case is unresolved and concerns consumer plans, not business ones. Source says: "misled customers to think they were required to pay extra for Copilot" https://www.itnews.com.au/news/accc-accuses-microsoft-of-misleading-27-million-australians-over-m365-fees-621312#:~:text=misled%20customers%20to%20think,pay%20extra%20for%20Copilot
reasoning:
What decided it: It takes real work to tell which product and licence you would be paying for: the name has changed repeatedly, and paid features come from a per-user add-on, metered Azure-billed agents and a promotional price.

This is a real, actively developed product from a vendor any procurement team can work with, but it needs a yellow verdict for now. The product has been renamed three times in about three years: Bing Chat Enterprise, then Copilot, then Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat, and now Microsoft Copilot Chat. The URL you gave already redirects to the latest name. The chat itself is free, but the paid features come from three places: a per-user Copilot licence, metered agents billed through an Azure subscription, and a time-limited discount. So before buying, pin down exactly which SKU, licence and metering terms you would be paying for. There are also security and data points to know. A DLP bug let Copilot Chat summarise emails labelled confidential (fixed in February 2026). EchoLeak was a critical zero-click flaw in Microsoft 365 Copilot (fixed on Microsoft's side in 2025). Web-search queries go to Bing, where Microsoft acts as an independent controller, outside the EU Data Boundary. Separately, an Australian regulator is suing Microsoft over how Copilot was bundled into consumer plans. Ask Microsoft for a written licence map (what the free tier covers, what the add-on covers, how agent metering is billed) and the DPA terms covering web grounding.

What would change the call: It would move up to green if Microsoft gave a stable name and a single written licence map: which features are free, which need the add-on, how agent metering is billed and capped, and how long the $18 price lasts. It would move down to red if the ACCC case ended in a court finding that Microsoft misled customers about Copilot pricing in business plans, or if a Copilot data-exposure incident turned up that Microsoft had not disclosed.

product: Bending Spoons portfolio (e.g. Evernote, WeTransfer, Vimeo, Brightcove, Meetup, StreamYard, FiLMiC Pro, komoot, AOL, Eventbrite, Airtable, Miro; Mailchimp pending)
green_flags:
- Bending Spoons is a large, audited business. Its SEC F-1 shows $1.31bn revenue in 2025, which supports its scale claims. Source says: "The company's revenue grew 95% year over year to $1.31 billion in 2025" https://fortune.com/2026/06/08/bending-spoons-italian-aol-evernote-wetransfer-files-us-ipo/#:~:text=The%20company%27s%20revenue%20grew,%241.31%20billion%20in%202025
- The company is listed on Nasdaq and actively buying established enterprise software; its first post-IPO deal was Airtable for $1.285bn in cash. Source says: "Bending Spoons has agreed to buy Airtable in an all-cash deal valuing the U.S. software firm at $1.285 billion" https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/04/bending-spoons-in-first-post-ipo-aquisition-with-1point3b-airtable-deal.html#:~:text=Bending%20Spoons%20has%20agreed,firm%20at%20%241.285%20billion
- The contracting entity can be identified: the footer names the operating company, its parent, its Milan address and its registry and VAT numbers. Source says: "Bending Spoons Operations S.p.A. | Sole shareholder company subject to the management and coordination of Bending Spoons S.p.A." https://bendingspoons.com/#:~:text=Bending%20Spoons%20Operations%20S.p.A.,of%20Bending%20Spoons%20S.p.A.
- Airtable's own newsroom confirms the acquisition is complete and that the owner commits to investing in product and support, which matches the Airtable card in the homepage carousel. Source says: "investing heavily in Airtable's product, customer support, and go-to-market capabilities" https://www.airtable.com/newsroom/airtable-joins-bending-spoons#:~:text=investing%20heavily%20in%20Airtable%27s,support%2C%20and%20go%2Dto%2Dmarket%20capabilities
yellow_flags:
- Independent reporting describes a pattern: Bending Spoons buys software companies and soon lays off most of their staff, as it did at Vimeo, Evernote and WeTransfer. Ask any acquired product for staffing and support commitments. Source says: "the equity firm is known for purchasing tech companies and aggressively cutting costs via layoffs" https://engadget.com/big-tech/vimeo-lays-off-most-of-its-staff-just-months-after-being-bought-by-private-equity-firm-184556023.html#:~:text=the%20equity%20firm%20is,cutting%20costs%20via%20layoffs
- The URL is a holding-company site that describes acquiring and integrating businesses. It has no product, pricing or contract to procure, so the buyer must identify the specific product and entity they would sign with. Source says: "We acquire businesses and integrate them into our central operating system of people, data, and technologies." https://bendingspoons.com/#:~:text=We%20acquire%20businesses%20and,people%2C%20data%2C%20and%20technologies.
- Trustpilot reviews of Bending Spoons (29 reviews, 1.7/5) repeatedly complain about steep price increases after acquisitions at Vimeo, Evernote and Harvest. The company does not reply. The sample is small, but the complaint keeps recurring. Source says: "Last year I paid $360 for Vimeo. This year I found a renewal price of $4,800" https://www.trustpilot.com/review/bendingspoons.com
- After buying Evernote, Bending Spoons laid off nearly all of its US and Chile staff in 2023, following an earlier round of 129 cuts. Source says: "laid off nearly all of Evernote's employees in the US and Chile" https://www.engadget.com/evernote-is-relocating-to-europe-after-laying-off-most-of-its-us-workforce-205012133.html#:~:text=laid%20off%20nearly%20all,the%20US%20and%20Chile
- In 2025, under Bending Spoons ownership, WeTransfer added a terms clause covering machine learning on uploaded content. It withdrew the clause after a backlash. Check data-use terms closely in any contract. Source says: "WeTransfer has also now amended its terms of service, removing any mentions of machine learning." https://thenextweb.com/news/how-wetransfer-reignited-fears-about-training-ai-on-user-data#:~:text=WeTransfer%20has%20also%20now,mentions%20of%20machine%20learning.
- TechCrunch confirms Vimeo layoffs soon after Bending Spoons acquired it. Bending Spoons would not say how many people were affected. Source says: "Vimeo, the video-hosting platform, is laying off some of its global staff" https://techcrunch.com/2026/01/22/vimeo-starts-layoffs-after-acquisition-by-bending-spoons#:~:text=Vimeo%2C%20the%20video%2Dhosting%20platform%2C,of%20its%20global%20staff
- The group's compliance page lists Italian legal and governance documents but no security certifications. SOC 2 or ISO 27001 evidence has to come from each product's own trust centre. Source says: "The following are links to documents and platforms designed to ensure Bending Spoons remains legally compliant:" https://support.bendingspoons.com/compliance#:~:text=The%20following%20are%20links,Spoons%20remains%20legally%20compliant%3A
reasoning:
What decided it: There is no product to buy at this URL, and the owner has a record of cutting staff and raising prices at the software companies it acquires.

Yellow: shortlist only after you pin down which Bending Spoons product you are buying and how this owner tends to treat products it acquires. The company itself is solid. It is listed on Nasdaq, files with the SEC, reported $1.31bn revenue in 2025, names its legal entity in full, and I found no regulator findings or breaches. The verdict comes from two things. First, bendingspoons.com sells nothing: it is a holding-company page, and what you would actually contract for is Evernote, Vimeo, WeTransfer, Airtable and so on. Second, the owner has a well-reported habit of deep layoffs soon after buying a company (Evernote 2023, WeTransfer 2024, Vimeo 2026), and users report steep price rises. Before committing, get from the specific product: multi-year price caps, the support and staffing commitment after acquisition, a data-use clause (remember the 2025 WeTransfer AI-terms episode) and the product's own SOC 2 or ISO 27001 report.

What would change the call: It would move to green if the buyer is pointed to one specific product (for example Airtable or Vimeo Enterprise) that has its own published SOC 2/ISO 27001 report, contractual price caps and a stated support and staffing commitment. It would move to red if a regulator or court finding against Bending Spoons or one of its products turned up, for example on unlawful data use or deceptive subscription practices.

product: PimEyes (face search / reverse image search engine)
vendor: PimEyes (originally Pimeyes Sp. z o.o., Poland; since 2021 owned by Giorgi Gobronidze via changing offshore entities)
green_flags:
- The product is real and long-running. It is widely covered, and the CEO speaks on the record about a small but working operation. Source says: "which he said has a staff of about 12 people" https://www.nhpr.org/2023-10-11/too-dangerous-why-even-google-was-afraid-to-release-this-technology#:~:text=which%20he%20said%20has,of%20about%2012%20people
- PimEyes stopped serving Russia after the 2022 invasion and later blocked access in 27 countries, so there is no sanctioned-market exposure. Source says: "All Russia-based biometrics searches are being rejected" https://www.biometricupdate.com/202205/pimeyes-launches-facial-recognition-affiliate-program-blocks-russian-requests-due-to-war#:~:text=All%20Russia%2Dbased%20biometrics%20searches%20are%20being%20rejected
yellow_flags:
- The contracting party is an offshore Dubai company with no register number, under UAE law. That leaves EU and US customers little practical recourse. Source says: "Suite No.1906, City Tower 2, Sheikh Zayed Road 94895 Dubai, United Arab Emirates" https://pimeyes.com/en/terms-of-service#:~:text=Suite%20No.1906%2C%20City%20Tower,Dubai%2C%20United%20Arab%20Emirates
- Illinois residents filed a BIPA privacy suit against the companies and individuals behind PimEyes. This report gives no outcome. Source says: "PimEyes invaded their privacy while collecting and scanning images of millions of Americans" https://www.biometricupdate.com/202305/amazon-immune-to-bipa-this-time-biometric-privacy-suit-filed-against-pimeyes#:~:text=PimEyes%20invaded%20their%20privacy,of%20millions%20of%20Americans
- A US senator wrote to the CEO over the tool's use to identify and dox immigration officers, and questioned whether its 'personal use' limits are enforced. Source says: "publicly accessible digital library of individuals' lives and likenesses in the wrong hands poses unthinkable risks" https://www.biometricupdate.com/202509/republican-senator-targets-overseas-facial-recognition-site-over-ice-doxing#:~:text=publicly%20accessible%20digital%20library,hands%20poses%20unthinkable%20risks
- Ownership has moved several times: founded in Poland, moved to the Seychelles in 2020 by an anonymous owner, then bought through a Dubai shell company in late 2021. Regulators have also opened proceedings. Source says: "Germany's privacy watchdog opened proceedings against PimEyes" https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PimEyes#:~:text=Germany%27s%20privacy%20watchdog%20opened%20proceedings%20against%20PimEyes
- Trustpilot shows a split rating (3.5 from 154 reviews, 38% one-star), with complaints about continued charges after cancellation. The company replies to few negative reviews. Source says: "PimEyes continued charging me for several months even though I had requested to cancel my subscription" https://www.trustpilot.com/review/pimeyes.com
- The homepage's scale claims contradict each other ('millions' vs '500K+' users, 99.5% vs 98% accuracy). The 'Trusted By Millions' press logos come from mostly critical coverage. Source says: "Join millions of users utilizing our advanced facial search engine to monitor their digital identity" https://pimeyes.com/en#:~:text=Join%20millions%20of%20users,monitor%20their%20digital%20identity
- The privacy policy names no security certification or auditor. It offers only a general statement about reviews. Source says: "We undergo regular legal and security reviews" https://pimeyes.com/en/privacy-policy#:~:text=We%20undergo%20regular%20legal%20and%20security%20reviews
red_flags:
- The Hamburg data protection authority concluded that PimEyes acted unlawfully on a GDPR access and deletion request. It took no enforcement action because the company sits in Dubai. noyb sued the authority in April 2026. Source says: "assumes that PimEyes acted unlawfully and should have responded to the complainant's access and deletion request" https://noyb.eu/node/1627#:~:text=assumes%20that%20PimEyes%20acted,access%20and%20deletion%20request
- Baden-Württemberg's data protection commissioner opened fine proceedings against PimEyes, the first anywhere. The core finding is that PimEyes processes biometric data to identify people, which the GDPR prohibits. Source says: "Das Vorgehen des Unternehmens wirft aus Sicht der Datenschutz-Grundverordnung erhebliche Fragen auf." https://netzpolitik.org/2022/bussgeldverfahren-aus-dem-laendle-pimeyes-droht-eine-millionenstrafe/#:~:text=Das%20Vorgehen%20des%20Unternehmens,Datenschutz%2DGrundverordnung%20erhebliche%20Fragen%20auf.
- Despite those findings, the homepage advertises 'GDPR Compliant' as a trust badge and claims GDPR compliance in its feature copy. Source says: "Bank-level encryption and GDPR compliance ensure your data stays secure" https://pimeyes.com/en#:~:text=Bank%2Dlevel%20encryption%20and%20GDPR,your%20data%20stays%20secure
- The vendor's own documents conflict on data retention. The homepage says uploads are never stored. The privacy policy keeps facial images from users without an account for 48 hours and keeps results for 30 days. Source says: "securely stored for 48 hours after the User not having account sends the photo" https://pimeyes.com/en/privacy-policy#:~:text=securely%20stored%20for%2048,account%20sends%20the%20photo
reasoning:
What decided it: European data protection regulators have found that PimEyes' face-search processing is unlawful, yet the vendor advertises itself as GDPR compliant and is based offshore, beyond their reach.

Red. PimEyes is a real, working face-search engine that has run since 2017, but no enterprise procurement team should shortlist it. The deciding ground is regulatory. The Hamburg data protection authority (DPA) concluded that PimEyes acted unlawfully. Baden-Württemberg opened fine proceedings because it found PimEyes processes biometric data to identify people, which the GDPR prohibits. Meanwhile the homepage shows a "GDPR Compliant" trust badge. The contracting party is an offshore Dubai company that, by the Hamburg DPA's account, does not answer regulators. It has about 12 staff, faces an Illinois biometric privacy (BIPA) class action and gets US Senate scrutiny over doxing. Its own documents contradict each other: the homepage says uploads are "never stored", while the privacy policy keeps them for 48 hours. Before any use, the buyer would need a lawful basis under GDPR/BIPA for searching third parties' faces, and the vendor offers nothing to support one.

What would change the call: To move up to yellow, the buyer would need to see a closed regulatory record: a published decision clearing PimEyes, or a resolved Baden-Württemberg proceeding and BIPA case. The vendor would also need a contracting entity inside the EU or US with a register number, and an independent security audit (ISO 27001 or SOC 2). Nothing more could push it further down; a published fine or court judgment would only confirm red.

- Rocket took over Vertica's dedicated team and customer base, according to independent trade press. Source says: "adding more than 600 customers and 170 employees." https://itbrief.com.au/story/rocket-software-completes-vertica-acquisition-from-opentext#:~:text=adding%20more%20than%20600%20customers%20and%20170%20employees.
